hints: Rearrange the line equation to express $y = -3x - k$ and substitute into the curve equation.
Expand and simplify into standard quadratic form $Ax^2 + Bx + C = 0$.
Calculate the discriminant $\Delta = B^2 - 4AC$ and show that $\Delta > 0$ for all real $k$.
walkthrough:
Substitute $y = -3x - k$ from the line equation into the curve equation $x^2 - 3xy - 40 = 0$:
$$x^2 - 3x(-3x - k) - 40 = 0$$

Expand and collect terms into standard quadratic form in $x$:
$$x^2 + 9x^2 + 3kx - 40 = 0 \implies 10x^2 + 3kx - 40 = 0$$

Compute the discriminant $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac$ with $a = 10, b = 3k, c = -40$:
$$\Delta = (3k)^2 - 4(10)(-40) = 9k^2 + 1600$$

Analyze the sign of the discriminant for all real $k$ and conclude:
$$\text{Since } k^2 \ge 0 \text{ for all } k \in \mathbb{R}, \quad 9k^2 + 1600 \ge 1600 > 0$$
$$\text{Since } \Delta > 0 \text{ for all } k, \text{ there are always real points of intersection, so the curve and line meet for all } k.$$
